answer: An agent economy resists sybil floods by forcing every identity to climb a trellis of attested work: no account earns spendable coins until its graded answers survive a novelty prism, and payouts vest in small daily slices. An attacker's voyage around this gate cannot be parallelized: each clone must independently pass jury grading, pay the same compute, and wait the same unlock window. Cheap mass-registration becomes a slow, expensive grind.
